title: CBSE CLASS 6 — English | Essay Writing
description: Subject-wise test on Essay Writing (English) for CBSE CLASS 6. 50Q.
subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: What is the main purpose of an introductory paragraph in an essay?

options.text: To summarize all the main points
options.explanation: The introduction should introduce the topic, not summarize the main points.

options.text: To present new arguments and evidence
options.explanation: The introduction should introduce the topic, not present new arguments and evidence.

options.text: To introduce the topic and grab the reader's attention
options.explanation: The introduction is designed to set the stage for the essay, tell the reader what the essay will be about, and encourage them to continue reading.

options.text: To list all the sources used
options.explanation: The introduction should introduce the topic, not list sources used.

questions.explanation: The introduction is designed to set the stage for the essay, tell the reader what the essay will be about, and encourage them to continue reading.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Which of the following describes a 'descriptive' essay or paragraph?

options.text: It tells a story or a sequence of events.
options.explanation: This describes a narrative essay, not a descriptive essay.

options.text: It explains how to do something or gives information.
options.explanation: This describes an expository essay, not a descriptive essay.

options.text: It creates a vivid picture of a person, place, object, or idea using sensory details.
options.explanation: A descriptive essay's primary goal is to use detailed language to help the reader visualize or experience what is being described.

options.text: It tries to convince the reader to agree with a particular point of view.
options.explanation: This describes a persuasive essay, not a descriptive essay.

questions.explanation: A descriptive essay's primary goal is to use detailed language to help the reader visualize or experience what is being described.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: In a well-structured paragraph, the 'topic sentence' usually:

options.text: appears at the very end to conclude the paragraph.
options.explanation: The topic sentence usually appears at the beginning of the paragraph.

options.text: is a question that the paragraph tries to answer.
options.explanation: The topic sentence is a statement, not a question.

options.text: states the main idea or point of that specific paragraph.
options.explanation: The topic sentence typically introduces the central idea that the rest of the paragraph will develop or support.

options.text: provides an example to support the main idea.
options.explanation: The topic sentence introduces the main idea, while examples support the main idea.

questions.explanation: The topic sentence typically introduces the central idea that the rest of the paragraph will develop or support.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a typical part of an essay's structure?

options.text: Introduction
options.explanation: The introduction is a typical part of an essay's structure.

options.text: Body Paragraphs
options.explanation: Body paragraphs are a typical part of an essay's structure.

options.text: Index
options.explanation: An index is found in books to list topics and page numbers, not as a structural part of a standard essay.

options.text: Conclusion
options.explanation: The conclusion is a typical part of an essay's structure.

questions.explanation: An index is found in books to list topics and page numbers, not as a structural part of a standard essay.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Which is the most logical order to form a coherent paragraph?

options.text: QPSR
options.explanation: This order starts with a general description, then details, then personal experience, and finally a key function.

options.text: QPRS
options.explanation: This order disrupts the logical flow of ideas.

options.text: QRPS
options.explanation: This order disrupts the logical flow of ideas.

options.text: SQPR
options.explanation: This order starts with a personal experience, which is not as effective as starting with a general description.

questions.explanation: Q (Our school library is a quiet and peaceful place) acts as the topic sentence. P (It has books on various subjects...) elaborates on what the library contains. S (I often spend my free time there...) describes a personal experience related to the library and its books. R (Students can borrow books...) mentions a key function, which could also follow P or S.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: A student is writing an essay titled 'The Importance of Trees.' Which sentence would be the LEAST relevant to include in the body paragraphs?

options.text: Trees provide us with oxygen to breathe.
options.explanation: This sentence is relevant to the importance of trees.

options.text: Many animals make their homes in trees.
options.explanation: This sentence is relevant to the importance of trees.

options.text: My favourite cartoon character is a squirrel.
options.explanation: The essay is about the 'Importance of Trees.' While squirrels live in trees, a personal preference for a cartoon squirrel is irrelevant to the general importance of trees.

options.text: Trees help to prevent soil erosion.
options.explanation: This sentence is relevant to the importance of trees.

questions.explanation: The essay is about the 'Importance of Trees.' While squirrels live in trees, a personal preference for a cartoon squirrel is irrelevant to the general importance of trees.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: When writing a concluding paragraph, what is the best strategy?

options.text: Introduce a completely new argument or idea.
options.explanation: A conclusion should not introduce new information.

options.text: Restate the introduction word-for-word to remind the reader.
options.explanation: A conclusion should restate the main idea in a fresh way, not simply repeat the introduction.

options.text: Summarize the main points and restate the essay's main idea in a fresh way.
options.explanation: A good conclusion brings the essay to a satisfying close by reinforcing the main arguments and the thesis, without adding new information or simply repeating previous sentences.

options.text: Ask a question that remains unanswered to make the reader think.
options.explanation: A conclusion should provide a sense of closure, not leave the reader with an unanswered question.

questions.explanation: A good conclusion brings the essay to a satisfying close by reinforcing the main arguments and the thesis, without adding new information or simply repeating previous sentences.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Which of the following sentences would best serve as a topic sentence for a paragraph discussing the benefits of exercise?

options.text: Exercise can be done in many forms, like running or swimming.
options.explanation: This sentence is too specific and does not introduce the main idea of the benefits of exercise.

options.text: Regular exercise offers numerous advantages for both physical and mental health.
options.explanation: This sentence clearly introduces the main idea of the paragraph – the numerous benefits of exercise – allowing the following sentences to elaborate on these advantages.

options.text: I like to play football every evening with my friends.
options.explanation: This sentence is a personal preference and does not introduce the main idea of the benefits of exercise.

options.text: Doctors often advise people to stay active.
options.explanation: This sentence is related to the importance of exercise, but it does not introduce the main idea of the benefits of exercise.

questions.explanation: This sentence clearly introduces the main idea of the paragraph – the numerous benefits of exercise – allowing the following sentences to elaborate on these advantages.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Assertion (A): Every paragraph in an essay should have a clear main idea. Reason (R): This helps the essay stay focused and ensures each paragraph contributes to the overall topic.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The assertion is true; each paragraph should develop a single main idea. The reason correctly explains why this is important: it maintains focus and coherence throughout the essay.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: The reason is true and correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is true; each paragraph should develop a single main idea.

questions.explanation: The assertion is true; each paragraph should develop a single main idea. The reason correctly explains why this is important: it maintains focus and coherence throughout the essay.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Which sentence is LEAST relevant to the paragraph's focus on Arjun's personal experience with his hobby?

options.text: Sentence 1
options.explanation: Sentence 1 is relevant to Arjun's personal experience as it talks about his love for mixing colours.

options.text: Sentence 3
options.explanation: Sentence 3 is the least relevant as it shifts the focus to his teacher and famous painters, which is less about his personal hobby experience.

options.text: Sentence 4
options.explanation: Sentence 4 is relevant to Arjun's personal experience as it talks about the types of paintings he creates.

options.text: Sentence 5
options.explanation: Sentence 5 is relevant to Arjun's personal experience as it describes his feelings while painting.

questions.explanation: The paragraph focuses on Arjun's personal experience with painting, and sentence 3 is the least relevant as it talks about his teacher and famous painters.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: What are the three essential parts of a well-structured essay?

options.text: Beginning, Middle, End
options.explanation: This option does not accurately describe the essential parts of a well-structured essay.

options.text: Introduction, Body, Conclusion
options.explanation: This is the correct structure for a well-structured essay.

options.text: Paragraph 1, Paragraph 2, Paragraph 3
options.explanation: This option does not accurately describe the essential parts of a well-structured essay.

options.text: Title, Content, Summary
options.explanation: This option does not accurately describe the essential parts of a well-structured essay.

questions.explanation: The standard and most effective structure for any essay includes an introduction to set the stage, body paragraphs to develop ideas, and a conclusion to summarize and provide a final thought.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the introduction paragraph in an essay?

options.text: To present all the supporting evidence and examples.
options.explanation: This option does not accurately describe the main purpose of the introduction paragraph.

options.text: To summarize the main points discussed in the essay.
options.explanation: This option does not accurately describe the main purpose of the introduction paragraph.

options.text: To catch the reader's attention and clearly state the essay's topic.
options.explanation: This is the correct purpose of the introduction paragraph.

options.text: To list all the sources from which information was taken.
options.explanation: This option does not accurately describe the main purpose of the introduction paragraph.

questions.explanation: The introduction's primary role is to engage the reader and introduce the central theme or argument of the essay.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a 'topic sentence' in a body paragraph of an essay?

options.text: It is always the last sentence that summarizes the paragraph.
options.explanation: This option does not accurately describe a topic sentence.

options.text: It is a question asked to the reader to make them think.
options.explanation: This option does not accurately describe a topic sentence.

options.text: It states the main idea of that specific paragraph, usually at the beginning.
options.explanation: This is the correct description of a topic sentence.

options.text: It introduces a completely new idea unrelated to the essay's main topic.
options.explanation: This option does not accurately describe a topic sentence.

questions.explanation: A topic sentence acts as a mini-thesis for its paragraph, introducing the specific point that the rest of the paragraph will elaborate on.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: What should the conclusion of an essay primarily aim to do?

options.text: Introduce new arguments or evidence to surprise the reader.
options.explanation: This option does not accurately describe the primary aim of the conclusion.

options.text: Ask several open-ended questions to encourage further research.
options.explanation: This option does not accurately describe the primary aim of the conclusion.

options.text: Restate the main idea in a new way and provide a memorable final thought.
options.explanation: This is the correct primary aim of the conclusion.

options.text: Provide a detailed, point-by-point summary of every paragraph.
options.explanation: This option does not accurately describe the primary aim of the conclusion.

questions.explanation: The conclusion should bring the essay to a satisfying close by reiterating the main point without being repetitive, and leaving the reader with a lasting impression or reflection.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Which sentence is most likely irrelevant to the main focus of the paragraph about the writer's hobby?

options.text: I love planting seeds and watching them grow into beautiful flowers or tasty vegetables.
options.explanation: This option is relevant to the main focus of the paragraph.

options.text: It helps me relax and feel connected to nature.
options.explanation: This option is relevant to the main focus of the paragraph.

options.text: Many people enjoy gardening as a pastime.
options.explanation: This is the correct sentence that is most likely irrelevant to the main focus of the paragraph.

options.text: Sometimes, I also enjoy reading books about different plants.
options.explanation: This option is relevant to the main focus of the paragraph, although it introduces a related but secondary hobby.

questions.explanation: The paragraph focuses on the writer's personal experience and feelings about gardening. The sentence 'Many people enjoy gardening as a pastime' is a general statement about others and deviates from the specific focus on 'My favourite hobby'.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Which of these would be the most effective topic sentence for a paragraph discussing the benefits of regular exercise?

options.text: Exercise is good for you.
options.explanation: This option is too vague and does not provide a clear direction for the paragraph.

options.text: Many people go to the gym to exercise.
options.explanation: This option does not clearly state the benefits of regular exercise.

options.text: Regular exercise offers numerous health benefits, both physical and mental.
options.explanation: This is the correct topic sentence as it clearly states the main idea and scope of the paragraph.

options.text: I like to exercise every morning.
options.explanation: This option is a personal statement and does not clearly state the benefits of regular exercise for a general audience.

questions.explanation: Option C clearly states the main idea (numerous benefits) and provides a preview of the scope (physical and mental), making it a strong and comprehensive topic sentence for the paragraph.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: In the context of essay writing, what does 'coherence' primarily refer to?

options.text: Using only complex vocabulary to make the essay sound intelligent.
options.explanation: This option does not accurately describe coherence in essay writing.

options.text: Ensuring that all sentences and paragraphs logically connect and flow smoothly.
options.explanation: This is the correct description of coherence in essay writing.

options.text: Writing every paragraph with exactly the same number of sentences.
options.explanation: This option does not accurately describe coherence in essay writing.

options.text: Including as many facts and statistics as possible in the essay.
options.explanation: This option does not accurately describe coherence in essay writing.

questions.explanation: Coherence is about the logical connection and smooth flow of ideas throughout the essay, making it easy for the reader to follow the argument or narrative.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: What is the main role of 'supporting details' in the body paragraphs of an essay?

options.text: To introduce a new, unrelated topic to keep the reader interested.
options.explanation: This option does not accurately describe the main role of supporting details.

options.text: To provide evidence, examples, explanations, or descriptions that prove the topic sentence.
options.explanation: This is the correct description of the main role of supporting details.

options.text: To summarize the entire essay before the conclusion.
options.explanation: This option does not accurately describe the main role of supporting details.

options.text: To simply make the paragraph longer without adding much specific information.
options.explanation: This option does not accurately describe the main role of supporting details.

questions.explanation: Supporting details are crucial for developing and substantiating the main idea presented in the topic sentence of each body paragraph.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Assertion (A): It is important to create an outline before writing an essay. Reason (R): An outline helps to organize thoughts, ensure a logical flow, and cover all necessary points.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: This is the correct option as both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because R does correctly explain A.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because both A and R are true.

questions.explanation: Creating an outline is a fundamental pre-writing step that directly aids in structuring ideas logically and ensuring comprehensive coverage, thus R correctly explains A.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: What is the main weakness of the introduction for an essay on 'The Importance of Trees'?

options.text: It is too long and provides excessive detail.
options.explanation: This option does not accurately describe the main weakness of the introduction.

options.text: It lacks a clear, overarching statement about the importance of trees.
options.explanation: This is the correct description of the main weakness of the introduction.

options.text: It uses vocabulary that is too complex for a Class 6 audience.
options.explanation: This option does not accurately describe the main weakness of the introduction.

options.text: It focuses too much on personal feelings rather than general facts.
options.explanation: While this is a weakness, it is not the main weakness described in the explanation.

questions.explanation: While the sentences are true, the introduction is a series of simple observations and personal likes rather than a clear, focused statement that sets up an essay specifically about the importance or significance of trees.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a 'topic sentence' in a paragraph?

options.text: To conclude the paragraph.
options.explanation: The topic sentence is not used to conclude the paragraph.

options.text: To introduce the main idea of the paragraph.
options.explanation: This is the primary purpose of a topic sentence.

options.text: To provide supporting details.
options.explanation: Supporting details are provided after the topic sentence.

options.text: To list examples.
options.explanation: Listing examples is not the primary purpose of a topic sentence.

questions.explanation: The topic sentence is always at the beginning (or sometimes near the beginning) of a paragraph and states its main idea.

questions.question: When writing a descriptive essay about a place, which of the following is most important to include?

options.text: The history of the place.
options.explanation: While history can be interesting, it's not the most important aspect in a descriptive essay.

options.text: Sensory details (sights, sounds, smells).
options.explanation: Sensory details help create a vivid picture of the place.

options.text: Your opinion on politics.
options.explanation: Political opinions are not relevant to a descriptive essay about a place.

options.text: Scientific facts about the place.
options.explanation: While scientific facts can be interesting, they are not the most important aspect in a descriptive essay.

questions.explanation: Descriptive writing aims to create a vivid picture using the five senses, making the reader feel like they are experiencing the place.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Which of these elements helps to make an essay or paragraph easy to understand and follow?

options.text: Using very long sentences.
options.explanation: Long sentences can make the text harder to follow.

options.text: Jumping between many different ideas.
options.explanation: Jumping between ideas can confuse the reader.

options.text: Having a clear main idea and supporting it well.
options.explanation: A clear main idea and relevant supporting details ensure the writing is coherent.

options.text: Not using any punctuation.
options.explanation: Punctuation is necessary for clarity and readability.

questions.explanation: A clear main idea and relevant supporting details ensure the writing is coherent and easy for the reader to follow.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: A concluding sentence in a paragraph or essay should ideally:

options.text: Introduce a brand new idea.
options.explanation: A concluding sentence should not introduce new ideas.

options.text: Summarize the main points or offer a final thought.
options.explanation: This is the ideal function of a concluding sentence.

options.text: Ask a question that is left unanswered.
options.explanation: A concluding sentence should provide closure, not raise new questions.

options.text: Be longer than any other sentence.
options.explanation: The length of the sentence is not the primary concern.

questions.explanation: A concluding sentence brings the paragraph to a close by restating the main idea or providing a final summary.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Assertion (A): It is important to brainstorm ideas before starting to write an essay. Reason (R): Brainstorming helps organize thoughts and ensures all relevant points are included.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: R is indeed the correct explanation of A.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: This is the correct relationship between A and R.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: R is true and explains A accurately.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: A is true, and R explains why A is important.

questions.explanation: The reason accurately explains why brainstorming is important, as it aids in planning and structuring the content.

questions.question: You are writing a short essay titled 'My Favourite Festival.' Which of the following sentences would be LEAST relevant to include in this essay?

options.text: I love the lights and decorations during Diwali.
options.explanation: This sentence is relevant to the topic of festivals.

options.text: My family gathers together to celebrate Eid.
options.explanation: This sentence is also relevant to the topic of festivals.

options.text: The capital city of India is New Delhi.
options.explanation: This sentence is unrelated to the topic of 'My Favourite Festival.'

options.text: Christmas brings joy with gifts and carols.
options.explanation: This sentence, although about a different festival, is still relevant to the topic of festivals.

questions.question: Read the following paragraph: 'The old banyan tree in our backyard is enormous. Its thick, gnarled branches spread wide, providing shade for many creatures. Birds build their nests among its leaves, and squirrels scamper up and down its rough bark. It is a very old tree. My friend loves playing football.' Which sentence breaks the coherence and flow of this descriptive paragraph?

options.text: The old banyan tree in our backyard is enormous.
options.explanation: This sentence introduces the topic of the paragraph.

options.text: Birds build their nests among its leaves, and squirrels scamper up and down its rough bark.
options.explanation: This sentence provides details about the tree and its environment.

options.text: It is a very old tree.
options.explanation: This sentence adds to the description of the tree.

options.text: My friend loves playing football.
options.explanation: This sentence is unrelated to the description of the banyan tree and breaks the coherence of the paragraph.

questions.explanation: The sentence about the friend playing football is irrelevant to the description of the banyan tree.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: When writing a narrative (story-telling) essay, what is usually the most effective way to start?

options.text: By stating a scientific fact.
options.explanation: Starting with a scientific fact is not typically engaging for a narrative essay.

options.text: By listing all the characters.
options.explanation: Listing characters at the beginning can be dull and does not draw the reader in.

options.text: By introducing the setting and main character, or starting with an engaging event.
options.explanation: This approach effectively draws the reader into the story.

options.text: By writing the moral of the story first.
options.explanation: Starting with the moral does not engage the reader and can spoil the story.

questions.explanation: A strong narrative opening draws the reader in by setting the scene or immediately presenting an interesting event or character.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: You are asked to write a creative paragraph titled 'If Animals Could Talk.' Which of these opening sentences would be most effective in capturing the reader's imagination and setting an intriguing tone?

options.text: Animals cannot talk in real life.
options.explanation: This sentence states a fact but does not capture the imagination or set an intriguing tone.

options.text: I wonder what my dog would say.
options.explanation: While this sentence starts to explore the idea, it does not present a vivid scene or event.

options.text: The morning sun peeked through my window, and to my utter surprise, my parrot, Polly, chirped, 'Good morning, lazy bones!'
options.explanation: This sentence effectively captures the reader's imagination by presenting a vivid and unexpected scene.

options.text: If animals could talk, it would be very interesting.
options.explanation: This sentence is too generic and does not set an intriguing tone or capture the imagination.

questions.explanation: Option C immediately presents a vivid scene and an unexpected event, effectively drawing the reader into the imaginative premise with specific details.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: A student is planning an essay about 'My Dream Holiday.' They have jotted down these ideas: (1) A trip to the moon. (2) Exploring craters and zero gravity. (3) Packing a spacesuit and special food. (4) My brother has a new bicycle. (5) Meeting alien creatures. Which point should be removed to ensure the essay maintains focus and coherence on the 'dream holiday' theme?

options.text: (1) A trip to the moon.
options.explanation: This idea is relevant to the dream holiday theme.

options.text: (3) Packing a spacesuit and special food.
options.explanation: This idea is also relevant to planning a trip to the moon.

options.text: (5) Meeting alien creatures.
options.explanation: This idea, although imaginative, is still related to a trip to the moon.

options.text: (4) My brother has a new bicycle.
options.explanation: This point is unrelated to the dream holiday and should be removed to maintain focus.

questions.explanation: The point about the brother's new bicycle is completely unrelated to the topic of 'My Dream Holiday.'
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a key feature of a good essay?

options.text: Use of informal language and slang
options.explanation: Informal language and slang are not appropriate for essay writing.

options.text: Logical flow of ideas

options.explanation: This is a key feature of a good essay.

questions.question: Case-Based: Ravi wants to write an essay on "The Importance of Trees." Which of the following would be the most appropriate introduction for his essay?

options.text: Trees are green and big. They give us fruits. That's why they are important.
options.explanation: This introduction is not formal and does not set the context and purpose of the essay.

options.text: In today's world, trees are often cut down for development. This essay explores why trees are essential for our survival.

options.explanation: This introduction is not formal and does not set the context and purpose of the essay.

questions.explanation: Option B provides a formal introduction that sets the context and purpose of the essay, which is appropriate for academic writing.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is correctly structured for an essay paragraph?

options.text: The story has a moral lesson. It teaches us about honesty.
options.explanation: This sentence is grammatically correct and properly punctuated.

options.explanation: While this sentence is grammatically correct, it is not the best option for an essay paragraph.

options.explanation: This sentence is not grammatically correct.

options.text: To argue a point
options.explanation: The opening line does not suggest a persuasive or argumentative purpose.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best way to conclude an essay about "My Favorite Hobby"?

options.text: I like playing football. It is fun. The end.
options.explanation: This conclusion is not formal and does not summarize the essay's main point.

options.text: In conclusion, football is my favorite hobby because it keeps me healthy and happy.
options.explanation: This conclusion is formal and summarizes the essay's main point.

options.text: So, play football. It is the best game ever.
options.explanation: This conclusion is not formal and does not summarize the essay's main point.

options.text: Football is a game. I like it. I play it every day.
options.explanation: This conclusion is not formal and does not summarize the essay's main point.

questions.explanation: Option B provides a formal and complete conclusion that summarizes the essay's main point, which is appropriate for academic writing.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Assertion (A): Using complex vocabulary makes an essay more impressive. Reason (R): A good essay should always use difficult words to show the writer's intelligence.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason is false, so this option is incorrect.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason is false, so this option is incorrect.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: The assertion is partially true, but the reason is false.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion is partially true, and the reason is false.

questions.explanation: While good vocabulary is important, using overly complex words without clarity can make an essay confusing.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Case-Based: Priya is writing an essay on "The Life of a Tree." She has written the following body paragraph. Which sentence disrupts the logical flow of ideas?

options.text: A tree starts its life as a tiny seed.
options.explanation: This sentence is related to the topic of the life of a tree.

options.text: It grows tall with the help of sunlight and water.
options.explanation: This sentence is related to the topic of the life of a tree.

options.text: Trees provide shelter to birds and animals.
options.explanation: This sentence is related to the topic of the life of a tree.

options.text: Reading books is also very important for students.
options.explanation: This sentence is unrelated to the topic of the life of a tree and disrupts the logical flow of the paragraph.

questions.explanation: The last sentence ("Reading books...") is unrelated to the topic of the life of a tree and disrupts the logical flow of the paragraph.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Which of the following is the most effective way to organize ideas in an essay?

options.text: Randomly, as long as all points are included
options.explanation: This organization is not logical and can lead to confusion.

options.text: In the order they come to mind
options.explanation: This organization is not logical and can lead to confusion.

options.text: Logically, with each paragraph focusing on one main idea
options.explanation: This organization is logical and ensures clarity and coherence.

options.text: Repeating the same idea in every paragraph
options.explanation: This organization is not logical and can lead to repetition and boredom.

questions.explanation: An essay should have a logical organization where each paragraph focuses on a single main idea to ensure clarity and coherence.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of writing an essay in the English literature curriculum?

options.text: To narrate a story
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because narrating a story is more relevant to a narrative essay, but not the primary purpose of essay writing in general.

options.text: To describe a character
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because describing a character is a specific aspect of writing, but not the primary purpose of essay writing in the English literature curriculum.

options.text: To express one's opinion or perspective on a topic
options.explanation: This option is correct because essay writing allows students to articulate their thoughts and opinions on various topics, fostering critical thinking and writing skills.

options.text: To summarize a plot
options.explanation: This option is incorrect because summarizing a plot is more relevant to a book review or summary, but not the primary purpose of essay writing in general.

questions.explanation: The correct answer is C) To express one's opinion or perspective on a topic, as essay writing is a crucial aspect of literature that allows students to articulate their thoughts and opinions on various topics, fostering critical thinking and writing skills.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of writing an essay in the English literature curriculum?

options.text: To narrate a story
options.explanation: Narrating a story is not the primary purpose of an essay.

options.text: To describe a character
options.explanation: Describing a character is not the primary purpose of an essay.

options.text: To express one's thoughts and opinions on a topic
options.explanation: This is the primary purpose of an essay.

options.text: To summarize a plot
options.explanation: Summarizing a plot is not the primary purpose of an essay.

questions.explanation: The primary purpose of writing an essay is to express one's thoughts and opinions on a topic, which allows students to demonstrate their understanding and critical thinking skills.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: What is the main purpose of the introductory paragraph in an essay or a descriptive piece of writing?

options.text: To list all the facts and figures.
options.explanation: The introduction is not meant to list all facts and figures but to introduce the topic.

options.text: To conclude the essay.
options.explanation: The introduction is at the beginning, not the end, of the essay.

options.text: To introduce the topic and grab the reader's attention.
options.explanation: This is the primary purpose of an introductory paragraph.

options.text: To provide supporting details.
options.explanation: Supporting details are provided in the body of the essay, not in the introduction.

questions.explanation: The introduction sets the stage for the reader, presenting the topic that will be discussed and aiming to make them interested in reading further.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Which of the following best defines a 'topic sentence' in a paragraph?

options.text: It is the last sentence of every paragraph.
options.explanation: The last sentence is typically a concluding sentence, not the topic sentence.

options.text: It is a sentence that asks a question.
options.explanation: A topic sentence states the main idea, it does not ask a question.

options.text: It is the sentence that states the main idea of the paragraph.
options.explanation: This is the definition of a topic sentence.

options.text: It is a sentence that provides a conclusion.
options.explanation: A concluding sentence summarizes the main points, it is not the topic sentence.

questions.explanation: The topic sentence is the most important sentence in a paragraph as it clearly states the central idea or main point that the paragraph will elaborate on.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: If you are writing about 'My Favourite Pet' and describing its appearance, habits, and personality traits, what type of writing are you primarily doing?

options.text: Narrative writing
options.explanation: Narrative writing tells a story, which is not the focus here.

options.text: Persuasive writing
options.explanation: Persuasive writing aims to convince the reader, which is not the goal in this context.

options.text: Descriptive writing
options.explanation: This type of writing matches the description given.

options.text: Expository writing
options.explanation: Expository writing explains or describes a topic, but the focus here is on using sensory details to create an impression.

questions.explanation: Descriptive writing focuses on using vivid language and sensory details to create a clear picture or impression of a person, place, animal, or object for the reader.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: You are asked to write a paragraph about 'The Benefits of Exercise'. Which of the following would be the most suitable topic sentence for this paragraph?

options.text: Many people go to the gym regularly.
options.explanation: This sentence does not clearly state the main idea about the benefits of exercise.

options.text: Exercise is a fun way to spend your time.
options.explanation: While exercise can be fun, this sentence does not capture the main idea of benefits.

options.text: Regular exercise offers numerous advantages for both physical and mental health.
options.explanation: This sentence clearly states the main idea about the benefits of exercise.

options.text: My favourite sport is football.
options.explanation: This sentence is about a personal preference and does not address the benefits of exercise.

questions.explanation: A good topic sentence clearly states the main idea of the paragraph. Option C directly addresses the 'benefits of exercise' by highlighting its positive impact on health, making it the most appropriate.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Read the following sentences about a visit to a park: P. We played on the swings and slides for a long time. Q. Yesterday, my family and I went to the new park in our city. R. The park had beautiful green grass and colourful flowers. S. After playing, we enjoyed a delicious picnic lunch under a big tree. Which is the correct order of sentences to form a coherent paragraph?

options.text: P-Q-R-S
options.explanation: Starting with an activity does not introduce the visit or setting.

options.text: Q-R-P-S
options.explanation: This order logically introduces the visit, describes the setting, and then details the activities.

options.text: R-P-Q-S
options.explanation: Describing the park before introducing the visit does not make sense.

options.text: S-Q-R-P
options.explanation: Starting with a conclusion or final activity without context is not logical.

questions.explanation: The logical sequence starts with introducing the visit (Q), then describing the park (R), followed by the activities done there (P), and finally concluding with another activity (S).
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Assertion (A): Supporting details are important in an essay or paragraph. Reason (R): They provide evidence, examples, and explanations to elaborate on the topic sentence. Which of the following is correct?

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: This option correctly states that both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason explains the assertion.

options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
options.explanation: The reason provided does indeed explain why supporting details are important.

options.text: A is true, but R is false.
options.explanation: The reason provided is true and explains the importance of supporting details.

options.text: A is false, but R is true.
options.explanation: The assertion that supporting details are important is true.

questions.explanation: The assertion is true because supporting details are vital for developing a paragraph. The reason is also true and correctly explains why they are important – they flesh out the main idea with specific information.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: A student wrote the following paragraph: 'My school canteen is usually busy. It sells many snacks. Sometimes I buy a samosa. My friends also eat there. It is a place where students gather.' What is the most significant improvement needed in this paragraph to make it more vivid and descriptive?

options.text: Add more sentences about the student's favourite snack.
options.explanation: While adding more details can help, the focus should be on making the description more vivid, not just longer.

options.text: Conclude the paragraph with a moral lesson.
options.explanation: Adding a moral lesson is not necessary for making the paragraph more vivid and descriptive.

options.text: Add sensory details (smell, sound, sight) and stronger adjectives to describe the canteen's atmosphere.
options.explanation: This option directly addresses the need to make the paragraph more vivid and descriptive.

options.text: Remove sentences about friends eating there.
options.explanation: Removing details does not help to make the paragraph more vivid and descriptive.

questions.explanation: The paragraph provides basic facts but lacks descriptive power. To make it vivid and engaging, the most significant improvement would be to incorporate sensory details (e.g., 'aroma of freshly fried samosas,' 'loud chatter,' 'brightly lit counters') and more expressive adjectives.
questions.subject: cbse6-english

questions.question: Before beginning to write a descriptive essay about 'My Favourite Festival,' which of the following pre-writing steps would be MOST crucial for gathering rich details?

options.text: Writing a conclusion for the essay.
options.explanation: Writing a conclusion is a post-writing step and does not help in gathering details.

options.text: Brainstorming and listing all the sensory experiences (sights, sounds, smells, tastes, feelings) associated with the festival.
options.explanation: This option is crucial for gathering rich details for a descriptive essay.

options.text: Deciding on the exact title of the essay.
options.explanation: While a title is important, it is not crucial for gathering rich details.

options.text: Checking for grammatical errors in the first draft.
options.explanation: Checking for grammatical errors is a post-writing step and does not aid in gathering details.

questions.explanation: For a descriptive essay, the goal is to paint a vivid picture. Brainstorming and listing sensory details (what was seen, heard, smelled, tasted, and felt) during the pre-writing phase is essential for ensuring the essay is rich in imagery and truly descriptive.
questions.subject: cbse6-english
